links.outcome: LLM answer quality vs experts on real-world clinical questions, rather than exam-style
links.effect: No significant quality difference between LLM and clinical experts (mean 3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); harmful in 13% expert vs 16% LLM answers (P=.63).
links.quote: There were no significant differences between the quality of the answers between LLM and clinical experts (mean scores of 3.38 vs 3.63; median 4.00, IQR 3.00-4.00 vs median 3.67, IQR 3.33-4.00; P=.26; Wilcoxon signed rank test).

links.outcome: LLM answer quality and harmfulness compared with senior radiation oncology experts on same questions
links.effect: Quality not significantly different (3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); potentially harmful 16% LLM vs 13% experts (P=.63).
links.quote: The answers were deemed potentially harmful in 13% of cases for the clinical experts compared with 16% of cases for the LLM (P=.63; Fisher exact test).

screen.reason: The study evaluated a medical LLM on real-world radiation oncology questions in an offline blinded reader study against human experts, assessing quality and harmfulness without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
